about.title: Glendora Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Glendora sits along a stretch of the 210 Freeway where local traffic mixes with Foothill commuters, and the city's public collision records show 236 injury crashes in the most recent final year, with 328 people hurt. Route 66 and Grand Avenue also see a steady share of these incidents, especially during the Tuesday afternoon window when reported crashes tend to climb. Whether your collision happened at a Grand Avenue intersection, on a Route 66 stretch through town, or merging near the 210, the aftermath usually looks the same: medical visits, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster who wants a recorded statement. We handle car accident claims directly. Our team can review the details of your crash, explain your options under California law, and handle communication with insurers on your behalf. There's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, though claims against a government entity — like certain road defect cases — can require notice in as little as six months. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash, though your share of fault reduces the amount. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to inflate your share of blame, which is why it's worth pausing before you give one.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, but insurers still push back hard on these amounts. Having someone document your injuries and losses properly from the start matters more than people expect.

items.question: I was in a crash on Grand Avenue and the other driver's insurer already called me. Should I give a statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company before speaking with an attorney. Insurers are trained to ask questions that can be used to shift fault onto you, even informally. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How do I find an attorney to handle my case?
items.answer: You can contact us directly for a free consultation. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case recovers money. There's no cost to you upfront, and you're never obligated to hire us.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Glendora car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, like the city or county, played a role in causing the crash — for example, through a road defect — a much shorter notice deadline may apply, sometimes just six months. It's worth confirming your specific deadline early.
